opportunities.title: THORChain Just Told Bitget No: The $388M Hack Where the 'Neutral' Rails Won
opportunities.why_now: THORChain is publicly refusing Bitget's request to block the hacker's addresses while the attacker actively swaps stolen ETH through it, exposing the protocol's laundering-by-design problem in real time.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/analysis: walk through the swap trail, quote THORChain's refusal, and argue why 'permissionless' infrastructure will always be the hacker's best friend — this is the third THORChain-adjacent incident in a year.

opportunities.title: Circle and Tether Froze the Bitget Hack Funds — Except the Money Was Already Gone
opportunities.why_now: Fresh reporting shows issuer freezes only caught a fraction of stolen funds before they slipped into DeFi/cross-chain rails, undercutting the 'stablecoins as a safety net' narrative.
opportunities.angle: Data-driven breakdown: how much got frozen vs. how much escaped, and why freeze powers are theater once funds hit a DEX or bridge — tie back to THORChain swap timeline.

opportunities.title: A Fake Blockchain Named GIWA Just Drained $2M — And DYORSWAP Users Never Checked
opportunities.why_now: A brand-new copycat-chain scam siphoned $2M by spoofing a real project's name on a DEX, a textbook case of the exact due-diligence failure your audience already expects.
opportunities.angle: Rapid-fire postmortem: how the fake network fooled users, the on-chain red flags that were visible before the drain, and a checklist for verifying chain legitimacy before bridging/swapping.

opportunities.title: Magic Eden's $5.7M Near-Miss Is Every NFT Wallet's Dirty Secret: Legacy Approvals
opportunities.why_now: Magic Eden barely rescued $5.7M in NFTs exposed by old, forgotten token approvals — a vulnerability sitting dormant in millions of wallets right now.
opportunities.angle: Actionable security piece: explain approval exploits in plain terms, show readers how to audit/revoke their own legacy approvals today, framed as 'you're probably exposed too.'

opportunities.title: Bitcoin's Quantum Clock Is Ticking Faster Than the Fixes: Inside the 79% Compute Cutdown
opportunities.why_now: StarkWare just slashed the compute estimate for breaking quantum-safe Bitcoin schemes by 79%, quietly moving the 'not our problem yet' timeline much closer.
opportunities.angle: Forward-looking security explainer: compare the three competing fixes, translate the 79% number into a realistic threat timeline, and argue why holders should care now, not in 2030.
